title: Claude or Astra? Which is better and what game engine do you use?
author: No_Departure7494
selftext: Google keeps saying Astra is better, even posts on here agree, yet many of the amazing finished products shared on this sub are from Opus.

comments.author: Bulky_Blood_7362
comments.body:
Opus 5.5 is the best currently.

The 3d models, gameplay, animations and vfx i get with it is crazy.

Astra and it's pricing/limits looks like a joke compared to opus

replies.author: dont-pull-a-druckman
replies.body: Which is nuts, cause it used to be you'd go to GPT if you wanted the most bang for your buck regarding tokens. I'd almost never hit the limits. Weird how they've flipped

replies.author: cdshift
replies.body: I think when comparing astra to fable  its closer in token usage. Opus is considered in their "mid tier" offering now

replies.author: Bulky_Blood_7362
replies.body: Yea in token usage, not in quality tho. Claude still wins miles ahead

replies.author: xxyxxyyyx
replies.body: How do you actually use opus inside unity like so it can create models assets and work in the scene?

replies.author: Bulky_Blood_7362
replies.body: Unity is the game engine, you make the models in blender

comments.author: Navadvisor
comments.body: I'm having a lot of luck with Astra at coding, but it looks like Opus has a better eye from all the comparisons I've watched on YouTube.

comments.author: yungastronot
comments.body: They're good at different things. I have both. But if I had to choose one right now it'd be Claude Opus 5.5.

comments.author: TallonZek
comments.body: I use both and they are about on par, at middle settings opus is better at using blender though.

replies.author: i_am_carver
replies.body: Do you have it give it access to blender somehow or can you just tell it to somehow use it? I know very little sorry.

replies.author: TallonZek
replies.body: You need to set up an mcp, and ideally a github repo as well, the good news is you can literally just ask claude to do it for you.

comments.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
comments.body:
Opus 5.5 is cheaper, has much better taste, creates better 3D models, and does most of everything better...

I think Astra is very competitive for things like "make an AI for this game". or "optimize this game". Clear specific complex tasks that don't require taste is where it might still hold the edge but even then i am not sure.

replies.author: xxyxxyyyx
replies.body: How do you actually use opus inside unity like so it can create models assets and work in the scene?

replies.author: DonNascobaro
replies.body: im guessing you use the blender MCP

replies.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
replies.body: I don't use it in unity i use it in Three.js

comments.author: Recoil42
comments.body:
Opus 5.5 is currently the best, hands down. 

OpenAI and Anthropic are changing blows month to month so that may change.

comments.author: Agreeable-Safety-360
comments.body: Also Astra had been nerfed to shit. Claude just got nerfed ( people have made real love trackers to view models getting nerfed in real time). Currently claude is still much better, even while being nerfed

comments.author: redditscraperbot2
comments.body: Astra can do the work and if you understand your project will it can do an admirable job. But it’s hard not to just recommend opus. It understands the essence of the job better and has a much more developed aesthetic sense compared to Astra, which is pretty important. Astra can dig deep and sometimes find things Claude overlooked, but it can also over engineer and create messy solutions that Claude ends up cleaning up.

comments.author: dilberry
comments.body: Claude is great at game design / building things. It can't do image gen though, and doesn't really make textures, etc. Characters, sprites, critters, and all those things will not look very good with Claude. ChatGPT is amazing at making images, sprite sheets, etc that you can give to Claude to implement. They work better together.

comments.author: necronomicoder
comments.body: Claude Opus 5.5 is substantially cheaper and better.  Not even close.  I have opus managing codex and it marks it's homework.

comments.author: MotivatedforGames
comments.body:
Astra has been amazing for me. I tried the 200$ claude sub and tried out Opus 5.5. I found it to be annoying to work with, assuming way too much, putting out bad outputs, being very condescending, and I stopped using it and was able to get it refunded on the spot. I dont understand reddits glaze for Claude.

Claude literally made me nauseous. Is it a political reason?

replies.author: ReindeerOk2009
replies.body: Claude is not condescending, what are you asking it to do to get condescending responses? And the outputs are certainly better than Astra

comments.author: MattMaxBuilds
comments.body: I use Claude models more for the creative side of things and Astra/Sol are my workhorses. So both. For games I mostly use Three.js/R3F with WebGPU lately, but I’m pretty engine agnostic.

comments.author: siberianmi
comments.body: Opus 5.5 is amazing with Godot and even on a $20 plan can get a ton of quality work done iterating on the game.

comments.author: sirpalee
comments.body:
You can do great with either to be honest. I like claude's ultracode mode though, I can setup a bunch of big tasks and it runs for a day or two. Perfect to run side projects while working.

Astra, even with the ultra mode, is more direct and finishes quicker. Hard to say which one needs more followups though.

comments.author: Monkeylashes
comments.body: Both

comments.author: Officialpolygrafix
comments.body: Claude Opus 5.5 / Unity.

comments.author: M4xs0n
comments.body: GPT-6.1 SOL most of the time now for coding, it’s just as capable as Astra and much, MUCH cheaper. Opus 5.5 is way better for Visual stuff like 3D Models tho

comments.author: teleport66
comments.body: Claude is creative and it has great taste and design skills for anything you throw at it including games. I still review everything with Astra and it founds a page of issues after every substantial change, I always do a reliability, backend, etc pass with Astra, which then is reviewed again by Opus. The best alternative is by far using both.

comments.author: Manifesto-Engine
comments.body: Claude 100%. OpenAI doesn't have anything close to it.

comments.author: Disastrous-Round-150
comments.body: GPT 6 Astra, no game engines or frameworks, 100% from scratch.

comments.author: No-Appointment-1652
comments.body: opus 5.5 gooooood😃

comments.author: TottallyNotToxec
comments.body: Sp no talk about sol 6.1? That shit is the goat. Favourite model for long running tasks so far

comments.author: Comet7777
comments.body: Opus has been working very well for me

comments.author: roach01gt
comments.body:
I design everything with Opus 5.5 then have it handoff the actual coding to Sol 6.1, then Opus reviews and iterates under this same method until it is satisfied. Then I take a look and provide my feedback. 

I’ve gotten much better results this way compared to going Astra only. But don’t sleep on imagen 2.5. Let Astra make art, let opus give feedback alongside your own.
